messages:
amal: Quick sync — want to align on design partner runway and clear exit criteria for the private beta. We need a short rubric we can share with prospects by EOD Friday.

rachel: +1. Do we want a separate rubric for Dedicated vs Private customers or one unified DP rubric?

sandeep: My vote: unified baseline + addendum for Dedicated (scale/SLA) and Private (networking/compliance). Keeps outreach simple.

amal: Agreed. Baseline should cover: onboarding time, integration signal (API + SDK), key workflow coverage, and quality regressions.

maria: Can we make onboarding time concrete? e.g., target: full integration + smoke traffic within 2 weeks for early partners.

james: 2 weeks seems fair for reference apps. For heavier infra (VPC/on-prem) call it 6-8 weeks with SRE support.

sandeep: For metrics, propose: 1) Integration time (days), 2) Latency percentile vs baseline, 3) Cost delta per 1k requests, 4) NPS on feature fit. All measured pre/post migration.

amal: Nice. Also add "feedback velocity": number of actionable issues per week and time-to-fix for P0/P1. That's our main success signal for product.

rachel: Drafting a one-pager now. Should include: purpose, timeline, commitments (what we ship vs what partner commits), communication cadence, and exit criteria.

amesages (dp-coordinator-bot): Reminder: DP intake form has questions about traffic profile, compliance needs, and integration owners. Link: https://redwood.internal/dp-intake

maria: On exit criteria — suggest two paths: graduated to GA (meets all thresholds for 4 consecutive weeks) OR graceful offboard (if partner can't proceed due to internal priorities). Need clear handoff steps for each.

james: For graduation thresholds proposal: 1) <1.5x baseline 95p latency, 2) <10% cost delta after config recommendations, 3) integration time <= target, 4) documented SLOs + runbook.

sandeep: Also require regression tests & 10% sample prompts passing our quality checks (or partner-specific eval).

amal: We should standardize the rollout phases: Intake -> Kickoff -> Integration -> Stabilization (observability + runbook) -> Graduation/Offboard. Each phase has deliverables and owner.

rachel: Who owns kickoff? Solutions eng or CS? I'm thinking SE leads technical kickoff, CS handles partner success metrics and cadence.

maria: SE lead during integration, CS owns stabilization and business signoff. Product owns quality/regression gating.

james: Can we add a lightweight weekly template for partner check-ins? 3 bullets: blockers, recently shipped, asks. Keeps meetings crisp.

sandeep: I'll make a checklist for the DP intake form to surface red flags early: legacy infra, compliance blockers, no integration owner, <1k monthly requests.

amal: Good. Rachel — when you post the one-pager, include a short FAQ snippet: what DP gets (priority support, early roadmap influence, credits) and what we expect (feedback cadence, test data, dev time).

rachel: Will do. I'll post a draft in #product later today and ping this thread for signoff.

maria: Quick note on incentives: small stipend + engineering hours + visibility at launch works better than just credits.

james: Agreed. Also list a mutual NDA and data handling agreement in the intake.

sandeep: Final ask: let's add an "abort criteria" — e.g., if integration stalls >8 weeks without clear next steps, trigger a formal offboard checklist.

amal: Perfect. If we can land the doc today, we can start outreach next week. Thanks all, will synthesize into the one-pager after Rachel posts initial draft.

rachel: Draft uploaded: https://redwood.share/dp-runway-onepager — please leave inline comments by EOD. :thumbsup:
